members.title: Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition
members.lead: Incumbent could turn defeat into another term in office as rival parties erect confected barrier to unseating him Israel election results – live updates Full report: Coalition talks loom in Israel Analysis: Rise of Palestinian parties will redraw political landscape Hours before the final results from Israel’s elections were in, several things were clear. Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition had lost its mandate, and the opposition had a firm majority. But most of Israel’s Jewish opposition ruled out governing with Palestinian-led parties, in the course of a racist election campaign in which Netanyahu painted Palestinian citizens as an enemy inside the state. Continue reading...

members.title: Coalition talks loom in Israel as Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs set to fall short of majority
members.lead: Projections show votes for Palestinian parties surged in a tight contest that drew highest turnout in decades Israel election results – live updates Analysis: Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscape Israel’s future hung in the balance on Wednesday as it became clear that Benjamin Netanyahu had lost his governing majority. His political fate now depends on whether opposition Jewish parties are prepared to forge a common front with Palestinian parties, whose support surged in Tuesday’s elections. The leader of the Jewish opposition bloc, the retired general Gadi Eisenkot, appeared to rule out such a broad coalition in a premature declaration of victory overnight for what he called a “Zionist majority”. members.title: Israel election results live: Qatar says accusations of election interference in Israel ‘ridiculous and dangerous’
members.lead: Netanyahu’s claim of interference in election also dismissed by Israeli police and opposition parties Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival, has warned political opponents against exploiting allegations of foreign interference in Israel’s election to delay the swearing-in of the next Knesset. In remarks posted on X, Eisenkot said: Israel must safeguard the integrity of the elections against any attempt at interference, spin and manipulation, and examine every complaint thoroughly. On the other hand, political actors must not be allowed to exploit the situation and affect the swearing-in date of the 26th Knesset.” Continue reading...

members.title: Israeli leader Netanyahu accused of using ‘ugly’ smear tactics to cling to power
members.lead: Prime minister claims Arab Israeli parties used foreign backing to steal elections, in which his coalition lost its majority • Israel election – latest updates Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which the prime minister’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority. Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel, supposedly funded by foreign money.
